summary: Championship decider in a monsoon. Lauda pulled out on lap two saying 'my life is worth more than a title'. Hunt survived punctures and mid-race panic to secure the World Championship in the pit lane.
Villeneuve vs Arnoux — the most famous wheel-banging duel in F1 history. Two cars, one line, laps of contact and slipstream madness for a podium place.
Three drivers still in the title fight arrived in Adelaide. Mansell's rear tyre exploded down the main straight at 300 km/h and Prost stole the championship with an empty tank.
Torrential rain, standing water and constant crashes. Prost refused to start beyond the formation lap. Senna won a race almost everyone thought should never have been run.
Senna's opening lap in the wet — passing four cars including Prost and Hill — is still called the greatest lap in F1. Constant tyre changes, dry lines vanishing, sublime car control.
The race after Imola and Senna's death. Wendlinger already in a coma, drivers in mourning, front two grid slots left empty in tribute. Schumacher won a hushed, uneasy Monaco.
Title decider. Schumacher clipped a wall, Hill dived down the inside, and they collided. Schumacher's damaged car took Hill out and clinched his first World Championship in controversial fashion.
Only three cars finished. Rain, oil and crashes eliminated almost the entire field. Olivier Panis won from 14th on the grid — Ligier's last F1 victory.
A 13-car pileup at La Source on lap one. Schumacher then rammed Coulthard while lapping him in fog and stormed to the pits accusing him of murder. Damon Hill won Jordan's first race.
Hakkinen's double-pass on Schumacher and Zonta at 300 km/h through Les Combes — going either side of a backmarker in one move — remains one of the cleanest, boldest overtakes ever filmed.
Rain came from nowhere on the last laps. Cars were spinning at every corner, Montoya beached, Coulthard slid off, and Michael Schumacher clung on to win in front of home fans.

Biblical rain, a river across the track at turn 3, cars aquaplaning off in convoy. Race red-flagged after Alonso's massive crash into debris; Fisichella declared winner days later in a paperwork drama.
Fernando Alonso, aged 21, became the youngest pole-sitter and race winner in F1 history at the time. Renault's turning point and a first sign of the era to come.
Rain turned the banked Indianapolis oval treacherous. Schumacher dropped to the back, then carved through the field in a wet-tyre masterclass to keep his title bid alive.

summary: Räikkönen dominated on flat-spotted tyres because rules forbade a change. The vibration finally ripped his suspension off on the last lap while leading — one of the cruellest endings in F1.
Michelin runners refused to race after tyre failures on the banking. All 14 Michelin cars peeled into the pits after the formation lap, leaving six Bridgestone cars to run a farce of a Grand Prix.
Rain in qualifying scrambled the grid. Räikkönen started 17th and passed Fisichella around the outside of 130R on the last lap to win — considered one of the greatest drives ever.

summary: A wall of water hit on lap one. Six cars slid off at the same corner into a gravel pit like a slapstick reel. Race red-flagged, Alonso and Massa duelled in the closing wet laps.
Massa crossed the line world champion. For 38 seconds the Ferrari pit celebrated. Then Hamilton passed Glock in the final corner of the final lap in the wet to take the title by one point.

summary: Massa won the inaugural Valencia street race but the day's talking point was a botched pit release that sent Massa into Sutil's path — a season-long trend of Ferrari pit chaos.
Race started late for TV, ended early for weather. A tropical storm turned the track into a lake, red-flagged before half distance. Button collected half points for one of his easiest wins.
Mark Webber launched off the back of Kovalainen at 300 km/h and somersaulted into the tyre wall. He climbed out unhurt in one of F1's most terrifying, survivable crashes.

The inaugural Korean GP started under safety car in torrential rain on an unfinished circuit that was still literally wet paint. Vettel led until his engine blew and Alonso stole the win and title lead.
The longest race in F1 history — 4 hours 4 minutes with a two-hour red flag for rain. Jenson Button pitted six times, was last on lap 40, and passed Vettel on the final lap for the win.
Vettel was defending on ancient tyres from Alonso and Button when a huge crash between Petrov, Alguersuari and Hamilton red-flagged the race, saving Vettel a certain double loss.
Alonso stormed from 11th to victory at home in front of a delirious Spanish crowd. Vettel's alternator failed while leading, Grosjean crashed while podium-bound — pure emotional overload.
Vettel spun on lap one and was last, facing off with Alonso for the title. Rain came, safety cars came, the radio broke. He fought back to sixth to win the championship by three points.
'Multi 21'. Vettel defied team orders and passed Webber for the win. Red Bull's internal cold war exploded on the podium and never really thawed.
Typhoon Phanfone raged. On lap 43 Jules Bianchi aquaplaned into a recovery crane at Dunlop. The sport changed forever: Virtual Safety Car, Halo, tighter marshalling. F1's darkest modern day.
Massa led early, then rain hit in the closing stint. Hamilton read the sky perfectly, pitted at the right lap and won at home while others slid off — a masterclass in timing.
Alonso and Räikkönen collided at the start, Alonso's McLaren pinned on top of Kimi's Ferrari in a shocking near-miss. Rosberg won under strategy pressure from Hamilton.
Rosberg and Hamilton, the two title contenders, took each other out on lap one. Enter Max Verstappen, 18 years old, first Red Bull race — he won on debut. F1's youngest winner ever.
Rain, red flags, and Verstappen went from 14th to 3rd in fifteen laps. A quadruple-wheel slide at 300 km/h that he casually caught was the moment he became a superstar.
Vettel deliberately drove into Hamilton behind the safety car. Multiple red flags, both Force Indias colliding twice, Ricciardo winning from tenth after starting the day behind three cars.
Vettel locked up out of the lead. The Red Bulls took each other out. Bottas got a puncture from debris while leading. Hamilton inherited a win from nowhere. Baku doing Baku things.
Vettel was cruising to victory at home in the dry. Rain hit. He crashed into a barrier at the Sachskurve. Hamilton, having started 14th, inherited the win. A title-defining moment.
Chaos on wet-dry crossovers. Almost every top driver spun or crashed at Turn 16. Kvyat on the podium for Toro Rosso, Verstappen winning after his own spin. Nobody knew who was where.
Verstappen bulldozed past Leclerc at Turn 3 with three laps to go. A three-hour stewards' hearing followed. The 'let them race' verdict shaped modern F1 racing rules.
Both Ferraris took each other out fighting for fourth. Two safety cars, Verstappen winning, Gasly holding off Hamilton for second in a Toro Rosso, Sainz on the podium after starting last.
Hamilton got a penalty for pitting under a closed pit lane. Leclerc crashed heavily. In the reshuffle Pierre Gasly, dumped by Red Bull a year earlier, won his first Grand Prix. Fairytale.
A freshly-laid, slippery track and cold rain. Lance Stroll on pole, cars spinning constantly. Hamilton drove a wet-tyre stint of 50 laps to clinch his seventh world championship.
Russell replaced Hamilton at Mercedes, dominated, then Mercedes fitted the wrong tyres in the pit stop. Perez went from last-lap spun to first-time winner in his final Racing Point race.
Wet start, Verstappen and Hamilton wheel-to-wheel through Tamburello, Russell crashing into Bottas at 320 km/h, red flag, Hamilton off through a gravel trap and back to second. Peak modern chaos.

summary: Rain-soaked start. Bottas rammed into the pack at Turn 1, taking out four cars. Everyone pitted for slicks except a bewildered Hamilton on his own. Esteban Ocon won his first race.

summary: Torrential rain. Officials sent the cars out for three laps behind the safety car, then awarded half points and declared it a race. F1's shortest ever GP; fans booed for hours.

Title decider. Hamilton dominant. A late safety car, a mis-applied lapped-cars rule, one shootout lap on fresh softs vs old hards. Verstappen passed Hamilton to become World Champion. Race director sacked.
Zhou Guanyu inverted at 240 km/h at Abbey on lap one, sliding under the catch fencing. Halo saved his life. Race restarted with Sainz taking his first F1 win in a thriller.
Rain-delayed start. Ferrari managed to lose the race for their pole-sitter Leclerc twice in one stop by radioing him to box after he'd already passed the pit entry. Perez won.
Three red flags in one race. Cars flying off at every restart, Alonso and Sainz colliding, a bizarre grid reshuffle before a two-lap sprint to the flag. Verstappen won a farce.
Rain hit before the formation lap. Cars pitted for wets on the way to the grid. Multiple safety cars, a red flag, Perez almost winning until a late shower reset the race. Verstappen prevailed.
